producer_report.summary:
I added a reading check, `check_records_measure`, that refuses a code or tests reading unless it includes a real-records criterion when it changes a measure computed from Athena's records. It fires on measure names such as landing time, keep rule, planning cost, refusal rates, check durations and throughput review figures, in the summary or a criterion. It also fires on a change to `status/throughput.rs` or `status/planning.rs`, so a code-health split of those modules needs the criterion too. The reading is accepted only if one behavior criterion names `real records`, an independent source of the range and an `expected range`. The accepted sources are `git log`, `history.json`, commit times, recorded check durations and landing record timestamps. Otherwise the refusal names the missing parts, cites the 2026-10-29 landing-time figures (0.1 and 273.8 minutes) and gives an example criterion. `git log` also needs an `Environment:` assumption. The example takes its range from `history.json` commit times and compares the `status --snapshot` output with it.

The check sits as one `step!` line after `check_history_fixture`. Its doc comment declares `expected 3% of newly refused readings` as an estimate, and the CHANGELOG has an entry.

I added one reader rule line, after shortening neighbouring lines so the section stays at its measured 3045 bytes. I added one planner line of at most 200 bytes. The tests are 6 unit tests in `reading.rs`, 12 corpus cases with 11 new input-form tags, a declared-intended test, and the brief size tests. `cargo fmt --check`, clippy with `-D warnings`, the full test suite, the policy scan and the mirrors test all pass.

The rule is checked by wording, so a criterion that holds the three phrases without running anything on real records still passes it. This job's own reading is among the newly refused readings.

criteria_check.criterion: crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs has exactly one added rule line in the reader brief and one in the planner brief stating that a change to a records-computed measure needs a criterion run against real records with an expected range from an independent source; Grep the diff shows one line each.
criteria_check.evidence: The rule text is built in the sub-modules, not in briefs.rs (briefs.rs only declares `mod planner; mod reader;`). So the lines are `READING_RULES` entry "Records measures: ..." in briefs/reader.rs and `REAL_RECORDS_RULE` in briefs/planner.rs, interpolated once in the Report. briefs.rs holds the tests: `the_reader_brief_names_each_reading_rule_in_one_short_line` asserts READING_RULES.len()==12 and exactly one line with `check_records_measure`, real records, expected range, independent source and landing time; `the_planner_brief_states_the_real_records_rule_once_within_its_bound` asserts one occurrence in the Report. Both pass. `git diff -U0 -- crates/athena-context/src/briefs/reader.rs crates/athena-context/src/briefs/planner.rs` also shows reader.rs '+' lines for shortened neighbouring entries, so the count rests on the test assertions.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-context`: the brief size test passes with both new lines, so the reader and planner briefs stay within their token budgets.
criteria_check.evidence: Ran `cargo test -p athena-context --quiet`: 133 passed, 0 failed. Measured before the change: reader rules section 3045 bytes, planner Report 1749 bytes. The reader test keeps `section.len() < 3150` and adds `section.len() <= READING_RULES_BASELINE_BYTES` (3045), so the section did not grow. The planner test asserts the rule is at most 200 bytes and `report.len() <= 1749 + rule.len() + 4`. The bound is the section limit, not the reader budget set (BudgetSet does not compose the brief text); the test comment says so.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a new test builds a code reading whose summary changes a records-computed measure (for example landing time) with only fixture-based criteria and asserts check_reading returns an error naming the missing real-records criterion.
criteria_check.evidence: `records_measure_without_real_records_criterion_is_refused` in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs builds a code reading with summary 'Fix the landing time shown by status' and a fixture-only criterion. It asserts gate_refuser == Some("check_records_measure"), and that the `accept` error holds "landing time", `real records`, independent source, `history.json`, `git log`, `expected range`, 0.1 and 273.8 minutes. It also asserts check_reading_text returns Refuse. `records_measure_refusal_names_what_is_missing` and `records_measure_words_and_paths_each_trigger_the_rule` cover missing parts, word variants, path triggers, splits and unchanged-measure readings. Ran `cargo test -p athena-core --lib records_measure`: 6 passed; full suite passed.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a companion test shows the same reading accepted once it adds a criterion naming real records, an independent source (git log or recorded check durations) and an expected range, and a reading not touching a records measure is unaffected.
criteria_check.evidence: `records_measure_with_a_real_records_criterion_is_accepted` adds a criterion naming real records, history.json commit times and an expected range to the same reading and asserts gate_refuser None, accept Ok and check_reading_text Accept. It also tries every independent-source phrase (including recorded check durations), a git log variant with an Environment: assumption, the path trigger, spelling variants and the example from the refusal text. `records_measure_leaves_unrelated_readings_alone` covers the default reading, docs, tests class, decline, question, content-only, drain throughput, CI wait time spent, records/throughput.rs, a deleted module and a wrapped or declared refusal-rate sentence. All pass.

criteria_check.criterion: The new check's doc comment in crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs or reading.rs states that it refuses more readings, the higher rate is intended, and declares `expected 3% of newly refused readings`.
criteria_check.evidence: The doc comment of `pub fn check_records_measure` in surveys.rs contains 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.' and 'expected 3% of newly refused readings', calls it an estimate, and cites 0.1 and 273.8 minutes. `records_measure_refusal_is_declared_intended` in tests/refusal_corpus.rs reads that doc comment, asserts these needles and that replay_declaration parses share Some(3). It passes.

criteria_check.evidence: New first item under [Unreleased] / Changed names `reading::check_records_measure`, states the rule, 2026-10-29, 0.1 minutes and 273.8 minutes, the history.json example, splits of the figure modules, 'higher refusal rate is intended' and 'expected 3% of newly refused readings'. The same test in refusal_corpus.rs asserts these needles in the changelog.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test`: all pass.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks. I ran `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`; all passed (the one clippy finding, vec_init_then_push, was fixed first).

open_issues: Criterion 1 names briefs.rs, but the lines live in briefs/reader.rs and briefs/planner.rs. briefs.rs holds the tests that pin them. Per the accepted plan.
checks.rs and refusal_corpus.rs are outside the reading's deliverable list but changed, per the accepted plan: the step! line lives in checks.rs, and the corpus needs a refusing case.
The check is lexical. It confirms the criterion exists but cannot confirm it runs on real records. The verifier runs it.
The 3% share is an estimate, not measured. This job's own accepted reading is among the newly refused readings, so the verification replay count includes it.

The 'refusal-rate-declaration-wrapped-line' corpus case may not exercise a wrapped bullet, because the request parser may take only the first line. The unit test in reading.rs covers the wrapped sentence directly.

The corpus case 'refusal-counts-status-from-5724053' uses the commit subject only. The deliverable list is a guess, status.rs and hestia.rs, and the source note says 'rebuilt from the commit subject'.
mistakes: The first draft of the new reader rule line made the reading rules section 98 bytes longer than its 3045-byte baseline. I then shortened neighbouring entries over three passes until it fit.
clippy::vec_init_then_push failed on the first corpus function I wrote. I fixed it by building the first case with let and starting the Vec from it.
learnings: The rule text for the reader and planner briefs is built in briefs/reader.rs and briefs/planner.rs. briefs.rs declares them as modules and holds only the tests.

The reader rules section was 3045 bytes and the planner Report 1749 bytes before this change. Both stay inside their bounds: the reader section did not grow, and the Report grew by the rule plus two newline bytes.
refusing_check's step! lines need a refusing corpus case (every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case), and INPUT_FORMS is a fixed-length array that must be bumped with new tags.
Clippy flags Vec::new() followed directly by push in test helpers; start the Vec with vec![first] instead.
This job's own reading (criterion 3 names 'landing time' with no real-records criterion) is refused by the new check, as the plan predicted. It is counted in the 3% estimate.
desires: A way to run cargo for measuring without a hook denying head, tail, grep and sed on its output; sizes had to be measured by temporarily failing an assert.
Build slots were busy for several attempts; a queue or a wait option would have saved retries.
